newsitem.title: USA: US DEBT FUND ALLOCATIONS STEADY AUG 12 WEEK - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: US DEBT FUND ALLOCATIONS STEADY AUG 12 WEEK - SURVEY.

text.p: U.S. money managers kept their portfolio allocations largely unchanged in the week ended August 12, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
Looking ahead, 8.0 percent of portfolio managers surveyed said they were planning to be active in the coming week, a drop from 17 percent registered the week ending August 5.
The bear/bull index fell slightly to 4.59 from 4.60 on an arithmetic basis. It rose to 4.53 from 4.42 on an asset-weighted basis.
"Market sentiment remains dour, as both bear/bull indices remain below a neutral reading of 5.0 percent," the report said.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio rose to 8.03 percent from 7.87 percent on an arithmetic basis and dropped to 5.61 percent from 6.14 percent on a weighted basis.
The survey's actual/target duration index rose to 97.26 percent from 96.86 percent on an arithmetic basis and rose to 100.32 percent from 99.01 percent on a weighted basis.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
